title: Optimize Conductor 3.0 — Live Fidelity Advisor and Distributed Quant Profiles (Release Notes)
author: Asha Menon
summary: Optimize Conductor 3.0 introduces the Live Fidelity Advisor, distributed quantization profiles, and a telemetry-normalization pipeline designed to reduce per-token cost while preserving response quality. This release focuses on runtime coordination between Optimize and the serving runtime, migration tooling for customers, and a new pricing addendum for fidelity-as-a-service. Rollout begins 2027-01-20 with progressive canaries.
content:
Purpose and scope:

This page documents the 3.0 release of Optimize Conductor (internal name: OC-3.0). The release bundles three product features and operational changes: (1) Live Fidelity Advisor (LFA), (2) Distributed Quantization Profiles (DQP), and (3) Telemetry Normalization v2 (TN-v2). The target audience is product, SRE, eng-serving-runtime, solutions engineering, and enterprise customers migrating to the new optimizer.

Highlights:
- Live Fidelity Advisor: a real-time signal generator that recommends per-request fidelity hints (quantization level, kv-cache retention, token budget preference) back to the serving runtime and SDK. LFA aims to lower unit cost by 10–30% on mixed conversational workloads while keeping quality regression below 1.5% on monitored eval sets.
- Distributed Quantization Profiles: allow customers to opt into per-tenant quant profiles that are coordinated across dedicated pools and private deployments. Profiles are stored in a signed, versioned manifest and can be roll-forward/rollbacked via the Optimize Console.
- Telemetry Normalization v2: reduces noise in cost attribution by 40% for batched streaming workloads; includes provenance tagging for per-prefix caching and fallback decisions.

Compatibility and footprint:
- Supported runtimes: Serving Runtime >= v5.4.0 (kernel and KV cache changes required).
- SDK changes: No breaking API changes. New thin SDK patch (client 2.5.0) exposes fidelity hints and local prefetch toggles.
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (immediate rollout), Dedicated (opt-in scheduled upgrade), Private (release bundle + migration script for on-prem appliances).

SLO & safety targets for rollout:
- Fidelity regression guardrail: end-to-end quality delta <= 1.5% as measured by tenant-controlled eval sets.
- Availability target during canary: 99.9% for canaries; 99.95% for full rollout windows.
- Reconciliation latency for advisor signals: median <= 120ms, p99 <= 450ms.

APIs and contract changes (developer-facing):
1) New SDK callbacks and headers (client 2.5.0):
   - x-rw-fidelity-hint: enum (high, balanced, low, custom).
   - fidelity_hint_callback(config) — library hook that surfaces LFA recommendations and decision metadata to the client app.
2) Admin endpoints (Optimize Console):
   - POST /orgs/:org/profiles/_apply — atomically apply a quant profile to a tenant.
   - GET /orgs/:org/profiles/:id/manifest — signed manifest for verification.

Operational rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal staging (2027-01-10 to 2027-01-17): run daily simulated traffic with chaotic fidelity toggles. Owners: eng-serving-runtime + Optimize infra.
2) Developer canary (2027-01-20 to 2027-02-03): opt-in for developer sandbox tenants. Monitor quality gates and cost curves. Owners: product + developer relations.
3) Controlled enterprise pilot (2027-02-07 to 2027-03-07): 5–8 enterprise customers invited; Dedicated customers can schedule upgrades; Private customers receive migration bundle. Owners: customer-success + eng-private-deployments.
4) Gradual ramp (from 2027-03-10): expand to broader hosted tenant population with automatic rollback thresholds configured. Owners: eng-sre + product.

Migration and customer guidance (checklist):
- Pre-migration:
  1. Ensure serving runtime >= v5.4.0 is available to your region or pool.
  2. Run the "OC-3 compatibility scanner" against your tenant workload samples (cli: rwd-compat-scan --profile oc3).
  3. Confirm client SDK 2.5.0 adoption schedule for your application teams.
- During migration:
  1. Enable LFA in balanced mode for 48–72 hours.
  2. Push a non-blocking sampling route (5% traffic) to collect fidelity decisions and retrain local pref cure heuristics.
  3. Validate no more than 1.0% increase in customer-reported error rates or timeouts.
- Post migration:
  1. Review the fidelity decision audit logs (Optimize Console -> Telemetry -> Fidelity Decisions).
  2. Consider customizing quant profiles for high-SLA routes.

Pricing and commercial notes:
- For hosted customers: LFA and TN-v2 included in Optimize Conductor base for all paying tiers. DQP is a paid add-on (per-tenant profile seats).
- DQP commercial model: $X/month per active profile + usage-based fraction for per-token quantization overhead. Finance has published the vendor-facing addendum (see related_pages).
- Trial path: customers can run a 30-day DQP pilot with up to 3 profiles; billing triggers only after pilot ends.

Monitoring and observability changes:
- New dashboards shipped under Optimize -> Fidelity Ops:
  - LFA Decision Distribution (bucketed by endpoint).
  - Profile Impact Heatmap (quality delta vs cost delta).
  - Telemetry Normalization Drift (per region).
- Alerts:
  - fidelity.regression.high — fires when end-to-end eval delta > 1.5% for 15m window. Severity: P1. Owner: eng-sre.
  - fidelity.advisor.latency.p99 — fires when p99 > 600ms for 5m window. Severity: P2. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Security and compliance notes:
- DQP manifests are signed with org-specific keys; private deployments must import org public keys into Appliance KeyStore.
- Telemetry Normalization v2 scrubs PII by default; customers with strict retention rules can opt into a redaction-only mode.

Operational runbooks (quick pointers):
- Rollback fidelity advisor to safe-mode: Console -> Fidelity -> Global -> safe-mode -> enable. This switches all hints to "balanced" and disables per-request experimentation.
- Emergency rollback of DQP: POST /orgs/:org/profiles/_rollback with profile_id. This immediately reverts to last stable manifest.

Known issues (v1):
- In some mixed-batch streaming scenarios (large batch sizes > 128 tokens on older kernels) the advisor may under-estimate cache retention leading to 5–8% higher latency spikes. Workaround: temporarily pin profile to "low" on heavy streaming routes.
- Private deployment migration script requires curl >= 7.68; older appliances will need an update before migration.

Telemetry and evaluation methodology (how we measure fidelity regressions):
- Eval sets: tenant-provided representative prompts + standard reference sets (conversational-commons-1000, summarization-200).
- Metrics: BLEU/ROUGE variants for structured tasks, embedding-sim delta for semantic parity, and human raters for a 200-sample audit per tenant.
- Measurement windows: rolling 7-day and 30-day with anomaly-detection baseline.

Release owner and contact info:
- Release owner: Asha Menon (Product Manager, Optimize).
- Technical lead: Evan Kim (Eng, Optimize Conductor).
- Oncall rotation for rollout window: optimize-oncall@redwood.internal.

Post-release follow-ups (action items):
1. Run a 30-day post-launch quality audit and publish a summary report by 2027-02-20. Owner: product.
2. Evaluate cost impacts per major customer segment and propose pricing adjustments if DQP trial uplift > 20% cost savings. Owner: finance + go-to-market.

Appendix: CLI snippets and example manifests
- Example apply command (hosted):
  rwd-optimize apply-profile --org acme --profile-file acme-dqp-v1.json --mode progressive

- Example profile manifest (text summary):
  - profile_id: acme-dqp-v1
  - model_compat: [rw-llama-13b-quant, rw-gpt-6b-8bit]
  - quant_strategy: dynamic-int8
  - fallback: balanced
  - signed_by: optimize-team@redwood.internal

Change log (brief):
- 2026-12-20: initial internal staging build (v3.0.0-rc.1).
- 2026-12-28: added TN-v2 telemetry pipeline improvements and SDK hook iteration.
- 2027-01-07: hardened rollout thresholds and added DQP manifest signing.
- 2027-01-15: final docs and publish.

Document history and maintenance:
- Owner: product/optimize. Update cadence: as-needed during rollout, quarterly thereafter.
